rationale: Round 0 built cleanly and passed correctness, so this round raises obfuscation pressure moderately while respecting dc's hot-loop structure (MultiWayMerge, SharedSortAggregate, ComputeGivenGroupbys are large, data-intensive kernels where aggressive control-flow rewriting would hurt). SUB stays near-universal: cheap arithmetic substitution with minimal correctness risk, so high weights across cost dimensions. BCF and FLA get high SecurityGain/DiversityGain to deepen control-flow flattening and bogus-edge coverage, but their RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights stay low-mid so the selector steers them away from the hottest inner loops, keeping overhead acceptable. SPLIT and IBR are cheap, low-risk diversifiers and are favored broadly to add structural heterogeneity between similar aggregate functions. ICALL is pushed up since indirect-call conversion substantially complicates static call-graph recovery in this call-heavy job-control/rbt code. IGV is kept mid-range: useful global-variable indirection for adc/jobcntl state, but with nontrivial correctness risk it is gated more conservatively. Net effect: broad cheap obfuscation everywhere, expensive transforms concentrated where features indicate they pay off.
